mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% YoY, the combination signals a mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative market performance.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction between PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent positive market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contractionary effect, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decrease does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.
